# Dependencies & Preparation

First we import the required libraries and set up the paths.
We also assume that the `coderdata` package is installed and available in the Python environment. 

We can then download the latest version of the coderdata dataset, using the following command in the terminal:

```{bash}
#| label: download data
#| warning: FALSE
#| eval: FALSE
#| echo: FALSE
coderdata download --local_path '/tmp'
```

We can now set up `reticulate` to interface with Python from R.


```{r}
#| label: imports-and-setup
#| warning: FALSE
#| echo: FALSE

# r libraries
library(reticulate)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)
library(GSVA) ##do to the enrichment statistics

# path setupd
data_dir <- "/tmp/"

#wd <- tempdir()
#setwd(wd)
reticulate::use_virtualenv('r-reticulate')
reticulate::import("coderdata")

# defines the python environment to use
py_require("coderdata")

# import the coderdata package from python
cd <- import("coderdata")


```


# Omics import
Now we are ready to load the datasets and format them for analysis. We will load the
 cell line datasets to load the relevant experimental,
drug, proteomic, and transcriptomic data for each dataset.

Note how this is done using the `reticulate` functionality to call Python functions from R via `cd$load(...)` and `datasets[[name]]$format(...)`.

```{r}
#| label: load-datasets
#| warning: FALSE
#| echo: FALSE


cell_lines <- c("ccle", "ctrpv2", "gcsi",
 "prism", "gdscv1", "gdscv2", "nci60",'fimm')

##actually only need to load 2 datasets
cell_lines <- c('gdscv2','ctrpv2')
exvivo <- c('beataml','bladder','pancreatic','sarcoma','colorectal','liver','mpnst','hcmi','cptac')

datasets <- list()

for (name in c(cell_lines, exvivo)) {
  datasets[[name]] <- cd$load(name, local_path = data_dir)
}

# experiments <- list()
# transcripts <- list()
# proteomics <- list()

# for (name in datasetnames) {

#     transcripts[[name]] <- datasets[[name]]$format(
#     "transcriptomics",
#     shape = "matrix",
#     metrics = "transcripomics"
#   )
#     proteomics[[name]] <- datasets[[name]]$format(
#     "proteomics",
#     shape = "matrix",
#     metrics = "proteomics"
#   )
# }
```


Now we have the transcripts data, each as a matrix. We can take a set of genes and identify 
specific drugs that are correlated with samples that are active in those.

## Panel A: Copy number

Let's plot copy number types across datasets

```{r}
#| label: plot-mutations

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

cl_cn <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cell_lines, function(ds){
  datasets[[ds]]$copy_number |>
    dplyr::rename(dataset = study)
})) |>
  distinct() #obviously this is kind of a pain and time consuming

ev_cn <- do.call(rbind, lapply(exvivo, function(ds){
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$copy_number 
  if (!is.null(cv))
    return(cv|> mutate(dataset=ds))
})) |>
  dplyr::select(-study)

comb <- rbind(cl_cn, ev_cn)
##now how can we plot these?
tot_counts <- comb |>
  group_by(dataset) |> summarize(total_genes = n_distinct(entrez_id))

print(tot_counts)
var_counts <- comb |> 
  group_by(copy_call, dataset, improve_sample_id) |> 
  summarize(genes = n_distinct(entrez_id))

ggplot(var_counts, aes(x=genes, fill = copy_call,y=dataset, alpha = 0.5)) + 
  ggridges::geom_density_ridges2() + 
  scale_fill_viridis_d()

```


## Panel B: Mutations
Now we can do the same with mutation types.

```{r}
#| label: mutations
#| 
cl_mu <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cell_lines, function(ds){
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$mutations
  cv[,c('entrez_id','variant_classification','improve_sample_id','study')] |> 
    dplyr::rename(dataset = study) 
})) |>
  distinct() #obviously this is kind of a pain and time consuming

ev_mu <- do.call(rbind, lapply(exvivo, function(ds){
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$mutations 
  #print(paste(names(cv),collapse=','))
  if (!is.null(cv))
    return(cv[,c('entrez_id','variant_classification','improve_sample_id')]|> 
      mutate(dataset=ds))
})) 

comb <- rbind(cl_mu, ev_mu)

comb |> group_by(variant_classification) |> 
  summarize(ndatasets=n_distinct(dataset)) 

comb |>  
  group_by(variant_classification, dataset, improve_sample_id) |> 
  summarize(genes_per_sample = n_distinct(entrez_id)) |> 
  group_by(variant_classification, dataset) |>
  summarize(mean_genes = mean(genes_per_sample)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x= variant_classification, y= mean_genes, fill = dataset)) + scale_y_log10()+geom_bar(stat='identity',position='dodge') + coord_flip()



```

This is too many, and most aren't in all datasets

```{r}

common <-  comb |> group_by(variant_classification) |> 
  summarize(ndatasets=n_distinct(dataset)) |> subset(ndatasets>5)

comb |> subset(variant_classification %in% common$variant_classification)|>
  group_by(variant_classification, dataset, improve_sample_id) |> summarize(n_genes = n_distinct(entrez_id)) |> ggplot(aes(x=n_genes, y=dataset, fill=variant_classification, alpha = 0.5)) + ggridges::geom_density_ridges2() +scale_x_log10() 
```

## Panel C: Transcriptomics
boxplot of values? 

```{r}
#| label: transcriptomics

cl_tr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cell_lines, function(ds){
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$transcriptomics
  cv[,c('entrez_id','transcriptomics','improve_sample_id','study')] |> 
    dplyr::rename(dataset = study) 
})) |>
  distinct() #obviously this is kind of a pain and time consuming

ev_tr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(exvivo, function(ds){
  #print(ds)
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$transcriptomics 
  if (!is.null(cv))
    return(cv[,c('entrez_id','transcriptomics','improve_sample_id')]|> 
      mutate(dataset=ds))
})) 

comb <- rbind(cl_tr, ev_tr)

ggplot(comb, aes(x=dataset, y = transcriptomics))+ 
  geom_boxplot() + scale_y_log10() 
```

Now can we make a UMAP?

```{r}

#library(ggfortify)
library(umap) 

nu <- comb |>
  tidyr::unite(dataset, improve_sample_id, col='sample',sep='-', remove=FALSE) 


cmat <- nu[,c('entrez_id','transcriptomics','sample')] |> 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from='sample',
    values_from='transcriptomics',values_fn=mean)

cm <- tibble::column_to_rownames(cmat,'entrez_id') |>
  drop_na()

pats <- nu[,c('sample','dataset')] |>
  distinct() #|>
  #subset(dataset!='beataml')

cols <- intersect(colnames(cm),pats$sample)
#pca <- prcomp(t(cm[,cols]))
#autoplot(pca, data=subset(pats, sample%in%cols),color='dataset')

cmm <- log2(cm + 1)
tumap = umap(t(cmm[,cols]), n_components = 2, random_state = 15) 

layout <- tumap[["layout"]] 
layout <- data.frame(layout) 
final <- cbind(layout, subset(pats, sample%in%cols)) 

ggplot(final, aes(x=X1,y=X2,col=dataset)) +geom_point() + 
  ggtitle("UMAP of log TPM of RNA-Seq datasets")

```

boxplot of values


Now try to do PCA

```{r}

nu <- comb |>
  tidyr::unite(dataset, improve_sample_id, col='sample',sep='-', remove=FALSE) 


cmat <- nu[,c('entrez_id','proteomics','sample')] |> 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from='sample',
    values_from='proteomics',values_fn=mean)

cm <- tibble::column_to_rownames(cmat,'entrez_id') |>
  drop_na()

pats <- nu[,c('sample','dataset')] |>
  distinct() #|>
  #subset(dataset!='beataml')

cols <- intersect(colnames(cm),pats$sample)
#pca <- prcomp(t(cm[,cols]))
#autoplot(pca, data=subset(pats, sample%in%cols),color='dataset')

cmm <- apply(cm,2,function(x) (x-mean(x))/sd(x))#cm#log2(cm + 1)
tumap = umap(t(cmm[,cols]), n_components = 2, random_state = 15) 

layout <- tumap[["layout"]] 
layout <- data.frame(layout) 
final <- cbind(layout, subset(pats, sample%in%cols)) 

ggplot(final, aes(x=X1,y=X2,col=dataset)) +geom_point() + 
  ggtitle("UMAP of Proteomics datasets")
```
